findings.criterion: no new workload ceiling is introduced: no run is aborted merely for being large, and a test
findings.detail: The evidence explicitly states the test does not drive a run past 239 requests (the 'previous flat-landing threshold' named in the criterion). The test uses max_iterations=200/land_after=40, running only 41 requests. No test in the file uses max_iterations=480 or drives past 239 requests. The evidence acknowledges: 'the specific "past the previous flat-landing threshold" sub-requirement of the test is not met at the literal 239-request level.'
findings.remediation: Add a test that drives a high-novelty run past 239 requests (e.g., max_iterations=480, land_after=250+) and asserts no RunawayToolLoopError is raised, directly demonstrating the guard does not introduce a workload ceiling at the previous flat-landing threshold.
findings.title: High-novelty run not driven past previous flat-landing threshold (239 requests)
